pathway.title: Wayfair Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, Wayfair has cut its debt and raised its earnings at the same time. Carrying total debt is USD 2,799 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 3,118 million at 2024-12-31, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is USD 853 million against USD 453 million in FY2024 [CP-1 handoff, leverage and metrics tables]. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.99x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the improvement being earnings-led, since debt fell 10.2% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 88.3%).

Second, liquidity is ample against the visible maturities. Wayfair holds USD 1,038 million of cash and USD 60 million of short-term investments, has USD 418 million of undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and owes USD 229 million of convertible notes in September 2027 and USD 800 million of secured notes in October 2029 [CP-1 handoff, liquidity and maturity tables]. Cash and investments cover the 2027 principal 4.8 times (Calculations). The remaining unsecured notes are convertible during the quarter ending 2026-12-31 with an if-converted excess over principal of USD 141 million, and the company may settle in cash, shares or both, so the cash call is within its control [CP-1 handoff, debt schedule; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact).

Third, the quality of the earnings measure decides how comfortable the leverage is. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity-based compensation and related taxes over the last twelve months, which is 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, and the company also paid USD 77 million of tax on net share settlement and USD 60 million of buybacks through financing in nine months 2026 [CP-1 handoff, definition review]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization of USD 549 million, total debt is 5.10x and net debt 3.10x; operating income of USD 283 million covers net interest expense of USD 156 million 1.81x (Calculations) (Analyst Interpretation).

Fourth, the cost of debt is rising even as the balance falls. Wayfair issued four fixed-rate secured series totalling USD 2,600 million since October 2024 and retired convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below, so stated coupons on USD 2,829 million of principal now total about USD 195 million a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 170 million; Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 5.02x and run-rate coupons 4.36x [CP-1 handoff, interest cover; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, the business is volume-led and U.S.-concentrated. The U.S. was 88% of FY2025 net revenue, Q3 2026 orders delivered rose to 11.0 million from 9.8 million while average order value fell to USD 311 from USD 317, and International Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of USD 54 million in nine months 2026 against U.S. earnings of USD 683 million [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model; CP-1 handoff, segments] (Documentary Fact). Negative working capital, with accounts payable of USD 1,213 million against inventories of USD 89 million, funds operations and would reverse in a volume decline; nine-month 2026 operating cash flow included a working-capital inflow of USD 64 million against an outflow of USD 76 million a year earlier [CP-1 handoff, cash flow reading].

Sixth, control and creditor protection rest on documents the pack does not contain. The co-founders and affiliates held 67.4% of voting power and 18.3% of the economic interest at year-end 2025, Class B stock is 15.3% of combined shares against a 10% automatic conversion level, no dividend has ever been paid, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or distribution evidence was found, but the indentures that would show capacity are not supplied [CP-1A handoff, ownership and governance table] (Documentary Fact; absence in the pack is not a finding of absence).

runs.text: Strengths. The first strength is deleveraging with earnings growth: last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million is up from USD 743 million in FY2025 and USD 453 million in FY2024, and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x from 4.40x and 6.88x [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is liquidity: USD 1,098 million of cash and short-term investments and USD 418 million of undrawn revolver exceed the USD 229 million due before 2029, which cash and investments alone cover 4.8 times (Calculations), and last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD 476 million, 55.8% of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the multiple is Analyst Interpretation). The third is a longer maturity profile: the 2026 and 2028 convertible notes are gone, the earliest remaining maturity is USD 229 million in September 2027, and the secured notes mature in 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2034 [CP-1 handoff, maturity table] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is repeat demand and growth: repeat customers placed 80.0% of Q3 2026 orders and net revenue rose 9.7% in the quarter, which supports revenue durability [CP-1A handoff; CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the release KPIs are management-calculated). The fifth is market access: the secured notes carry fair values between 98.9% and 102.9% of principal at 2026-09-30 (CP-1 handoff, debt schedule), consistent with continued access to secured debt markets (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. The first weakness is thin and adjusted earnings: net income over the last twelve months is a loss of USD 160 million, operating income plus depreciation and amortization is USD 549 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 2,804 million [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is rising fixed interest, as set out in the fourth key finding, which leaves less room if earnings slip [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The third is demand and concentration risk: a discretionary category, 88% U.S. revenue, a loss-making International segment and a single small-parcel carrier [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is working-capital and seasonality sensitivity: first-quarter operating cash flow was negative in both years printed, and the 2026 working-capital inflow may not repeat [CP-1 handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The fifth is that the claim stack is secured-heavy: secured notes are 91.9% of principal and share first-priority liens with the revolver, so the unsecured convertible notes rank behind them and structurally behind subsidiary liabilities, which matters for any loss given default analysis that later modules perform (mechanic only) [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Documentary Fact). The sixth is control and information: founder voting control, no covenant ratio reported, no ratings and no guidance mean that downside protection cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; the missing datapoints are the covenant definition and reported ratio, executed indentures, the proxy statement and ratings, as set out in Gaps).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no merger, acquisition, sponsor buyout or divestiture transaction in the pack, and the context holds no deal terms, so the transaction type is capital structure refinancing, completed, with no pending transaction. Documentary status is that every debt action below is complete as of the Q3 10-Q signed on 2026-11-04. The issuer of each secured series is Wayfair LLC, a subsidiary of Wayfair Inc., under indentures with the guarantors named therein, including Wayfair Inc., and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association as trustee and notes collateral agent (10-K page:121-122; Q2 10-Q page:12). The accepted financial base gives the amounts, coupons and maturities, which are not repeated in full here.

New debt issues in the period covered are four. First, 800 million of 7.250% senior secured notes due 2029 were issued on 2024-10-08 (10-K page:121). Second, 700 million of 7.750% notes due 2030 were issued on 2025-03-13 alongside the amended and restated credit agreement that provides the 500 million revolver maturing 2030-03-13 (10-K page:119, page:121). The 10-K states the use: on 2025-03-14 the company repurchased 578 million of 2026 convertible notes in connection with the issuance, and on 2025-05-09 it used the remaining proceeds with cash to repurchase 80 million of 2025 notes and 118 million of 2026 notes (10-K page:128). Third, 700 million of 6.750% notes due 2032 were issued on 2025-11-07 (10-K page:121); the pack does not state a use of proceeds, and the repurchase of 210 million of 2027 notes on 2025-11-12 for 375 million cash (10-K page:128) is close in time but is not linked to the issue by the filing, so no link is asserted. Fourth, 400 million of 7.125% notes due 2034 were issued on 2026-05-18, and the company used the proceeds with cash on hand on 2026-06-29 to settle the remaining 444 million of 2028 convertible notes after a redemption notice of 2026-05-14 (Q3 10-Q page:41, page:14-15). For the 2029 series the pack gives no use of proceeds.

The liquidity effect of the 2026 actions, from the accepted financial base, is that nine-month 2026 net cash on debt principal and extinguishment was 585 while operating cash flow was 506 and cash fell by 438 to 1,038. The effect on leverage is that carrying total debt fell from 3,272 at year-end 2025 to 2,799 and total debt to company-defined Adjusted EBITDA was 3.28x on the last-twelve-month figure of 853. The mechanism for creditors is as follows. Replacing convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below by secured notes at 6.750% to 7.750% raises fixed interest; the accepted base puts stated coupons on outstanding debt at about 195 a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of 170. It lengthens maturities, since the earliest remaining maturity is the 229 million 2027 convertible notes. It adds secured claims that share first-priority liens with the revolver, while the remaining convertible notes are unsecured and structurally subordinated. Convertible notes retired for cash above principal convert dilution into a cash cost: cash paid, including accrued interest and fees, was 375 for 210 of principal in 2025 and 247 for 145 in 2026 (Calculations), with extinguishment losses of 165 and 102 equal to the difference to carrying value. Shares were also issued in settlement: 0.9 million on the 2027 notes and 4.5 million on the 2028 notes (Q3 10-Q page:14-15). The 2027 notes themselves became convertible for the quarter ending 2026-12-31 and the filing says conversion may be settled in cash, shares or a combination at the company's election (Q3 10-Q page:13), so the remaining unsecured claim carries a cash call that the company controls through the form of settlement. Recovery prospects appear here as a mechanic only: secured and unsecured claims have different positions against the same asset base, and the pack gives no valuation or recovery analysis.

On the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, last-twelve-month earnings to Q3 2026 are 853 million, up from 743 million in FY2025 and 453 million in FY2024, and total debt at carrying amount fell from 3,272 million at 2025-12-31 to 2,799 million at 2026-09-30. The reader is a credit committee. Required decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. This module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion.

"CP-1 handoff" means a figure taken from the accepted financial base. Each fact row carries one of four categories: Documentary Fact (the cited source states it), Management Language (management's characterisation, quoted and not adopted), Analyst Interpretation (a reading of cited evidence) and Insufficient Information (the evidence is missing and the missing datapoint is named). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wayfair Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated, Boston-headquartered online home-goods retailer listed on the New York Stock Exchange (10-K page:1, page:9). It has no financial sponsor and the pack contains no merger, acquisition or sponsor transaction. The business sells through six brand storefronts, ships most orders directly from roughly 20 thousand suppliers' warehouses, and is adding its own warehouses, delivery network and a small physical store base (10-K page:9-14). The U.S. segment was 88% of FY2025 net revenue (10-K page:10). Ownership is public but control is concentrated: Class B stock carries ten votes per share, and at year-end 2025 the co-founders and their affiliates held about 18.3% of the economic interest and 67.4% of the voting power (10-K page:62).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For a creditor the transaction history that matters is capital structure change, not a deal. Since October 2024 the company issued four series of fixed-rate senior secured notes through its subsidiary Wayfair LLC totalling 2,600 million, entered into an amended and restated 500 million revolving credit facility, and used cash and the new issues to retire convertible notes that carried lower coupons and whose if-converted value exceeded principal at 2025-12-31 (10-K page:130). The effect, set out in the accepted financial base, is lower total debt and a maturity profile with nothing due in the rest of 2026 or in 2028 and 229 million due in 2027, at the price of higher fixed interest and a secured claim stack that ranks ahead of the remaining unsecured convertible notes. Five qualifications bound the view: the executed indentures and credit agreement are not supplied; two of the four issues have no stated use of proceeds in the pack; the 2026 proxy statement, which carries board and compensation detail, is not supplied; no credit rating is supplied; and the pack gives no management guidance. Nothing after the cutoff is used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no merger, acquisition, sponsor buyout or divestiture transaction in the pack, and the context holds no deal terms, so the transaction type is capital structure refinancing, completed, with no pending transaction. Documentary status is that every debt action below is complete as of the Q3 10-Q signed on 2026-11-04. The issuer of each secured series is Wayfair LLC, a subsidiary of Wayfair Inc., under indentures with the guarantors named therein, including Wayfair Inc., and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association as trustee and notes collateral agent (10-K page:121-122; Q2 10-Q page:12). The accepted financial base gives the amounts, coupons and maturities, which are not repeated in full here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues in the period covered are four. First, 800 million of 7.250% senior secured notes due 2029 were issued on 2024-10-08 (10-K page:121). Second, 700 million of 7.750% notes due 2030 were issued on 2025-03-13 alongside the amended and restated credit agreement that provides the 500 million revolver maturing 2030-03-13 (10-K page:119, page:121). The 10-K states the use: on 2025-03-14 the company repurchased 578 million of 2026 convertible notes in connection with the issuance, and on 2025-05-09 it used the remaining proceeds with cash to repurchase 80 million of 2025 notes and 118 million of 2026 notes (10-K page:128). Third, 700 million of 6.750% notes due 2032 were issued on 2025-11-07 (10-K page:121); the pack does not state a use of proceeds, and the repurchase of 210 million of 2027 notes on 2025-11-12 for 375 million cash (10-K page:128) is close in time but is not linked to the issue by the filing, so no link is asserted. Fourth, 400 million of 7.125% notes due 2034 were issued on 2026-05-18, and the company used the proceeds with cash on hand on 2026-06-29 to settle the remaining 444 million of 2028 convertible notes after a redemption notice of 2026-05-14 (Q3 10-Q page:41, page:14-15). For the 2029 series the pack gives no use of proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity effect of the 2026 actions, from the accepted financial base, is that nine-month 2026 net cash on debt principal and extinguishment was 585 while operating cash flow was 506 and cash fell by 438 to 1,038. The effect on leverage is that carrying total debt fell from 3,272 at year-end 2025 to 2,799 and total debt to company-defined Adjusted EBITDA was 3.28x on the last-twelve-month figure of 853. The mechanism for creditors is as follows. Replacing convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below by secured notes at 6.750% to 7.750% raises fixed interest; the accepted base puts stated coupons on outstanding debt at about 195 a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of 170. It lengthens maturities, since the earliest remaining maturity is the 229 million 2027 convertible notes. It adds secured claims that share first-priority liens with the revolver, while the remaining convertible notes are unsecured and structurally subordinated. Convertible notes retired for cash above principal convert dilution into a cash cost: cash paid, including accrued interest and fees, was 375 for 210 of principal in 2025 and 247 for 145 in 2026 (Calculations), with extinguishment losses of 165 and 102 equal to the difference to carrying value. Shares were also issued in settlement: 0.9 million on the 2027 notes and 4.5 million on the 2028 notes (Q3 10-Q page:14-15). The 2027 notes themselves became convertible for the quarter ending 2026-12-31 and the filing says conversion may be settled in cash, shares or a combination at the company's election (Q3 10-Q page:13), so the remaining unsecured claim carries a cash call that the company controls through the form of settlement. Recovery prospects appear here as a mechanic only: secured and unsecured claims have different positions against the same asset base, and the pack gives no valuation or recovery analysis.

fields.value: Issuer: Wayfair Inc. (issuer id w), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, with Q3 2026 as the current period, FY2025 as the prior period and USD as the reporting currency. This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the accepted financial base and the business and transaction context, using the upstream handoffs only, and gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. The evidence cutoff is 2026-11-05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This module reads no new source text; every figure comes from the handoffs below, which were checked against these pinned files.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wayfair Inc. is a better credit than it was two years ago, but it is still a thin-margin, discretionary-demand retailer whose leverage looks moderate only on management's own earnings measure. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt fell to USD 2,799 million and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA to 3.28x from 6.88x in FY2024, with USD 1,098 million of cash and investments, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before September 2027. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity compensation, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortization the ratio is 5.10x. What decides the outcome is whether U.S. order growth keeps converting into earnings faster than fixed interest is rising.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, Wayfair has cut its debt and raised its earnings at the same time. Carrying total debt is USD 2,799 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 3,118 million at 2024-12-31, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is USD 853 million against USD 453 million in FY2024 [CP-1 handoff, leverage and metrics tables]. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.99x (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the improvement being earnings-led, since debt fell 10.2% and Adjusted EBITDA rose 88.3%).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, liquidity is ample against the visible maturities. Wayfair holds USD 1,038 million of cash and USD 60 million of short-term investments, has USD 418 million of undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and owes USD 229 million of convertible notes in September 2027 and USD 800 million of secured notes in October 2029 [CP-1 handoff, liquidity and maturity tables]. Cash and investments cover the 2027 principal 4.8 times (Calculations). The remaining unsecured notes are convertible during the quarter ending 2026-12-31 with an if-converted excess over principal of USD 141 million, and the company may settle in cash, shares or both, so the cash call is within its control [CP-1 handoff, debt schedule; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, the quality of the earnings measure decides how comfortable the leverage is. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 293 million of equity-based compensation and related taxes over the last twelve months, which is 34.3% of Adjusted EBITDA, and the company also paid USD 77 million of tax on net share settlement and USD 60 million of buybacks through financing in nine months 2026 [CP-1 handoff, definition review]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization of USD 549 million, total debt is 5.10x and net debt 3.10x; operating income of USD 283 million covers net interest expense of USD 156 million 1.81x (Calculations) (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, the cost of debt is rising even as the balance falls. Wayfair issued four fixed-rate secured series totalling USD 2,600 million since October 2024 and retired convertible notes with coupons of 3.50% and below, so stated coupons on USD 2,829 million of principal now total about USD 195 million a year against last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 170 million; Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 5.02x and run-rate coupons 4.36x [CP-1 handoff, interest cover; CP-1A handoff, transaction summary] (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the business is volume-led and U.S.-concentrated. The U.S. was 88% of FY2025 net revenue, Q3 2026 orders delivered rose to 11.0 million from 9.8 million while average order value fell to USD 311 from USD 317, and International Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of USD 54 million in nine months 2026 against U.S. earnings of USD 683 million [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model; CP-1 handoff, segments] (Documentary Fact). Negative working capital, with accounts payable of USD 1,213 million against inventories of USD 89 million, funds operations and would reverse in a volume decline; nine-month 2026 operating cash flow included a working-capital inflow of USD 64 million against an outflow of USD 76 million a year earlier [CP-1 handoff, cash flow reading].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, control and creditor protection rest on documents the pack does not contain. The co-founders and affiliates held 67.4% of voting power and 18.3% of the economic interest at year-end 2025, Class B stock is 15.3% of combined shares against a 10% automatic conversion level, no dividend has ever been paid, and no priming, uptiering, drop-down or distribution evidence was found, but the indentures that would show capacity are not supplied [CP-1A handoff, ownership and governance table] (Documentary Fact; absence in the pack is not a finding of absence).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The first strength is deleveraging with earnings growth: last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million is up from USD 743 million in FY2025 and USD 453 million in FY2024, and total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 3.28x from 4.40x and 6.88x [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is liquidity: USD 1,098 million of cash and short-term investments and USD 418 million of undrawn revolver exceed the USD 229 million due before 2029, which cash and investments alone cover 4.8 times (Calculations), and last-twelve-month free cash flow is USD 476 million, 55.8% of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the multiple is Analyst Interpretation). The third is a longer maturity profile: the 2026 and 2028 convertible notes are gone, the earliest remaining maturity is USD 229 million in September 2027, and the secured notes mature in 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2034 [CP-1 handoff, maturity table] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is repeat demand and growth: repeat customers placed 80.0% of Q3 2026 orders and net revenue rose 9.7% in the quarter, which supports revenue durability [CP-1A handoff; CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact; the release KPIs are management-calculated). The fifth is market access: the secured notes carry fair values between 98.9% and 102.9% of principal at 2026-09-30 (CP-1 handoff, debt schedule), consistent with continued access to secured debt markets (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. The first weakness is thin and adjusted earnings: net income over the last twelve months is a loss of USD 160 million, operating income plus depreciation and amortization is USD 549 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 853 million, and the stockholders' deficit is USD 2,804 million [CP-1 handoff] (Documentary Fact). The second is rising fixed interest, as set out in the fourth key finding, which leaves less room if earnings slip [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The third is demand and concentration risk: a discretionary category, 88% U.S. revenue, a loss-making International segment and a single small-parcel carrier [CP-1A handoff, Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact). The fourth is working-capital and seasonality sensitivity: first-quarter operating cash flow was negative in both years printed, and the 2026 working-capital inflow may not repeat [CP-1 handoff] (Analyst Interpretation). The fifth is that the claim stack is secured-heavy: secured notes are 91.9% of principal and share first-priority liens with the revolver, so the unsecured convertible notes rank behind them and structurally behind subsidiary liabilities, which matters for any loss given default analysis that later modules perform (mechanic only) [CP-1 handoff; CP-1A handoff] (Documentary Fact). The sixth is control and information: founder voting control, no covenant ratio reported, no ratings and no guidance mean that downside protection cannot be measured (Insufficient Information; the missing datapoints are the covenant definition and reported ratio, executed indentures, the proxy statement and ratings, as set out in Gaps).

fields.value: The downside chain, with observable triggers, starts with a slowdown in U.S. demand (initiating condition). The first operational break would be falling orders delivered or lower average order value, which the release reports each quarter, forcing more advertising per order. The financial transmission is lower Adjusted EBITDA and a reversal of the 64 working-capital inflow as payables of 1,213 unwind against inventories of 89. The consequences are lower cash than the 1,038 held, less cover than 5.02x, and higher leverage, with the arithmetic reference points that LTM Adjusted EBITDA at the FY2025 level of 743 gives total debt of 3.77x and at the FY2024 level of 453 gives 6.18x (Calculations; these are reference levels, not forecasts). Refinancing then matters from 2029, when 800 of secured notes mature at market rates. Triggers to watch: quarterly orders and average order value, Adjusted EBITDA margin against 6.9%, cash against 1,038, the settlement election on the 2027 notes, and covenant certificates when obtained.
